L1 - Mojo Language (Python-family syntax + systems programming)
Specialize before instantiation - C++ templates evolved
Direct MLIR dialect access from Mojo source
Mojo as syntactic sugar for MLIR operations
L3 - KGEN Compiler Framework (MLIR Core - not linalg/StableHLO dialects)
Mojo parses directly to LIT MLIR dialect
Pre-bound parametric IR - reflectable by MAX GC
First language built ground-up on MLIR design principles - Mojo is to MLIR as C is to ASM
L4 - MAX Graph Compiler (JITGraph - MLIR-based AI inference stack)
Structured kernels from LIT kernel introspection
Memory planning - kernel inlining - weight registry
JIT compile packaged kernels - emit Mojo
No GC rebuild - introspect Mojo kernel signatures
DAG of executable kernels - cross-kernel fusion
Multi-level cache: model / GC IR / Mojo IR
L5 - Modular Platform / MAX Engine (inference + deployment)
L6 - Unified Hardware Abstraction (democratize AI compute)
Parametric IR before instantiation - same source multi-target
Step 1: Parse Mojo source - semantic analysis - traits/parameters resolved
Step 2: Emit parametric LIT MLIR - ops/types with compile-time attributes
Step 3: Specialize/instantiate for target + param values - mlir_op lowering
Step 4: MLIR Core progressive lower - LLVM IR - target machine code
Step 5: AOT binary or JIT at MAX runtime - concurrent execution on device
Standalone kernel OR packaged for MAX Graph Compiler introspection/fusion
Vision doc: parametric metaprogramming + MLIR Core + MAX framework
Execute MEF on CPU/GPU/accelerator via MAX Engine
Cross-kernel fusion - memory planning - zero-cost inlining
Stdlib: Apache 2.0 (open) - Compiler: proprietary today, OSS fall 2026
MAX core written entirely in Mojo - largest Mojo codebase
L7 - Design Position (AI-era systems language on MLIR)
Python productivity + systems performance + parametric kernels + graph-level fusion via MAX
Init path: write Mojo kernel/struct - parametric compile to LIT - package for MAX or AOT binary
Step path: Graph API model.mlir - MOGG fuse - MGP JIT - MEF execute on heterogeneous hardware
